claims.text: At fixed alloy composition, rapid quenching from the homogenization temperature suppresses nanoprecipitate formation relative to slow cooling.
Rapid quenching suppresses compositional segregation along grain boundaries relative to slow cooling.
Suppressing nanoprecipitates and grain-boundary segregation through rapid quenching retains greater toughness than slow cooling.
Cantor-type equiatomic HEAs homogenized between 900°C and 1200°C can have a uniform, single-phase FCC microstructure.
The proposed controlled change is cooling rate alone, comparing rapid quenching with slow cooling from the same homogenization temperature.
A controlled atmosphere is needed to prevent oxidation from confounding the comparison.
Nanoprecipitate density and distribution and grain-boundary compositional segregation are the structural mediators governing toughness retention.
Rapid quenching limits the diffusion kinetics required for nanoprecipitate nucleation and growth.
Rapid quenching limits the diffusion kinetics required for compositional segregation.
Slow cooling permits diffusion and consequently promotes nanoprecipitate formation and segregation.
Intergranular nanoprecipitates act as crack-initiation sites.
Crack initiation at intergranular nanoprecipitates reduces overall toughness.
Rapidly quenched specimens will have a more homogeneous microstructure than slow-cooled specimens.
Rapidly quenched specimens will have significantly higher fracture toughness than slow-cooled specimens.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold for similar single-phase FCC HEAs processed between 900°C and 1200°C under controlled atmospheres.
The proposed behavior may not apply to markedly different compositions or phase constitutions or when environmental degradation such as oxidation is active.
Cooling-rate-dependent changes in dislocation density could also contribute to the observed toughness difference.

The hypothesis is falsified if slow-cooled specimens show no statistically significant increase in nanoprecipitates or segregation, or if their fracture toughness equals or exceeds that of rapidly quenched specimens.
